'''Kesoram Industries Limited''' is an Indian industrial company which produces rayon and related products such as viscose  [[rayon]] and filament yarn.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kesoram Industries Ltd |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/KSRM.NS/ |publisher=Reuters |access-date=5 February 2025}}</ref> It was once part of the BK Birla Group.

== History ==
Kesoram Industries Limited started its business as Kesoram Cotton Mills in 1919. After a partnership, the first rayon plant was built in 1959 under the name Kesoram Rayon. Shortly after the plant was built, the company also started the production of tires and cement under the brand name [[Birla Tyres]] and Birla Shakti Cement respectively. In 1986, another cement plant, known as Vasavadatta Cement, was commissioned by it at [[Sedam]], [[Gulbarga district]], [[Karnataka]]. The name of the company was changed to Kesoram Industries Limited on 9 July 1986. Since then, Kesoram Industries listed on four stock exchanges: the [[National Stock Exchange of India]], the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]], the [[Calcutta Stock Exchange]], and the [[Bourse de Luxembourg]].

Kesoram Industries entered into a joint venture with Maharashtra Seamless Limited and Dhariwal Infrastructure Private Limited in 2012 for working a coal block allocated to it by the Central Government in [[Maharashtra]].<ref>{{Cite news|url = http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/kesoram-industries-ltd/stocks/companyid-13474.cms|title = Kesoram Inds. |work = The Economic Times|access-date = 23 August 2015}}</ref>

During 2014–15, the company sold a tyre plant to [[JK Tyres]].<ref>{{Cite news|url = http://profit.ndtv.com/news/earnings/article-kesoram-industries-q4-net-marginally-up-at-rs-349-crore-1411150|title = Kesoram Industries Q4 Net Marginally Up At Rs 349 Crore|work = NDTV Profit|access-date = 25 May 2016}}</ref> In 2018, Kesoram Industries [[demerger|demerged]] its tire manufacturing business [[Birla Tyres]], as part of a debt reduction plan.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kesoram to demerge tyre division, help to pare Rs 1000cr debt |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/kesoram-to-demerge-tyre-division-help-to-pare-rs-1000cr-debt-118120400888_1.html |access-date=20 August 2024 |work=Business Standard}}</ref> Birla Tyres later filed for [[insolvency]] and was taken over by a consortium led by Himadri Speciality Chemicals and [[Dalmia Group|Dalmia Bharat Refractories]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Birla Tyres set to roll again, acquisition finalised by consortium of Himadri and Dalmia |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/business/birla-tyres-set-to-roll-again-acquisition-finalised-by-consortium-of-himadri-and-dalmia/cid/1977074 |access-date=20 August 2024 |work=Telegraph India}}</ref>

In 2019, after the death of [[Basant Kumar Birla]], his daughter Manjushree Khaitan became the chairperson of Kesoram Industries.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manjushree Khaitan named Kesoram Industries' Chairman |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/manjushree-khaitan-named-kesoram-industries-chairman/article28594719.ece |access-date=20 August 2024 |work=BusinessLine |date=19 July 2019 |language=en}}</ref> In 2024, Khaitan died after a brief illness.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kesoram Industries Chairperson Manjushree Khaitan Dies At 68 |url=https://www.ndtvprofit.com/business/kesoram-industries-chairperson-manjushree-khaitan-dies-at-68 |access-date=20 August 2024 |work=NDTV Profit |date=16 May 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, Kesoram Industries announced that it would demerge and sell its 10.75 MTPA cement business to [[UltraTech Cement]] for {{INRconvert|5379|c}} in an all-stock deal.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Aravindh |first1=Sai |title=UltraTech To Buy Kesoram Industries' Cement Business For Over Rs 5,300 Crore |url=https://www.ndtvprofit.com/business/kesoram-to-merge-cement-business-with-ultratech |access-date=20 August 2024 |work=NDTV Profit |date=30 November 2023 |language=en}}</ref> The sale is expected to complete by the end of 2024, leaving Kesoram Industries with its rayon and transparent paper packaging businesses held by its subsidiary Cygnet Industries.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kesoram's cement business demerger into UltraTech Cements may be completed by December |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/business/kesoram-industries-cement-business-demerger-into-ultratech-cements-may-be-completed-by-december/cid/2032769 |access-date=20 August 2024 |work=Telegraph India}}</ref>

== Business ==
Kesoram Industries Limited has one major division:<ref>{{Cite news|url = http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/announcements/others/kesoram-industries-ltd-reply-to-clarification-sought-by-the-exchange/article7512808.ece|title=Kesoram Industries Ltd reply to clarification sought by the exchange |work = Businessline|date = 7 August 2015}}</ref>

=== Present business ===
* '''Kesoram Rayon''' - Established in 1959, Kesoram Rayon is a viscose rayon filament yarn and cellophane paper manufacturing unit. Situated on the banks of the Ganges, the factory has over 2,700 employees and 52 spinning machines, with an installed capacity of 6,500 MT per annum.

=== Former businesses ===
* '''[[Birla Tyres]]''' - Birla Tyres was first established in 1991 as part of Kesoram Industries Limited. It later collaborated with tyre manufacturer [[Pirelli]] in the production and development of its tyres.
* '''Birla Shakti Cement''' - Under the cement division of Kesoram Industries Limited, Birla Shakti manufactured and sold cement. The division operated two cement manufacturing plants located at Sedam, Karnataka (the Vasavadatta Cement Plant) and Basantnagar, near [[Ramagundam]] in [[Telangana]] (the Kesoram Cement Plant).<ref>{{Cite news|url = https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/kesoram-industries-ltd/summary/329|title = Kesoram Inds. Summary|work = India Infoline |access-date = 7 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url = http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/Vasavadatta-Cement-to-enhance-capacity/article20240860.ece|title = Vasavadatta Cement to enhance capacity |work = Business Line|access-date = 8 May 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url = http://www.dnaindia.com/business/report-kesoram-ind-eyes-stronger-foothold-in-cement-market-2488036|title = Kesoram Ind eyes stronger foothold in cement market|work = DNA India|access-date = 30 June 2017}}</ref>

==Recent developments==
In December 2025, the [[Birla family]] exited Kesoram Industries following the sale of their promoter stake to Frontier Warehousing Limited.<ref>{{cite news |title=Birlas exit Kesoram Industries |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/cement/birlas-exit-kesoram-industries/articleshow/125791180.cms|work=The Economic Times |date=December 2025 |access-date=5 February 2025}}</ref>
